items.requirement: Authoritative language specifications cover compilation, execution, artifacts, embedding, debugging, coroutines, ownership, and capabilities.
Exactly one governing architecture exists and translations do not introduce alternate decisions.
Frozen contracts cover semantic plans, target plans, artifacts, ownership, coroutines, executor conformance, runtime ABI, generation, and performance.
Every changed contract anchor and its digest are updated atomically and pass contract verification.
Historical design records are non-governing while valid historical test and commit evidence remains auditable.
Current architecture surfaces no longer present early bytecode, dual semantic lowering, universal executable bytecode, or JIT as the product architecture.
Early VM emission and mode-specific legality or pipeline ownership are absent.
Durable plans contain no target or compiler process pointers.
Backends do not reconstruct ownership, suspension, layout, or call decisions.
Missing plan facts fail closed without fallback.
Legacy Xaot value-representation and function-ABI owners are absent.
AOT owns no private semantic tags or object behavior.
C emission performs no semantic, type, name, shape, or spelling inference.
Generic lowering cannot hide a missing native plan behind a fallback.
Default tagged registers, tagged call frames, and VM-only place representations are absent.
Legacy opcodes, dispatchers, prototypes, chunks, serializers, and loaders are absent.
Legacy XRC source, build, cache, install, example, and test routes are absent.
Unsupported execution cannot be converted into a null result.
Coroutine execution retains no hidden semantic VM stack.
The VM owns no operation semantics or name-based dispatch.
Header, layout, destructor, and extent formulas each have one owner.
Overlapping bridge, clone, and rebox implementations are absent.
Arbitrary runtime graph sharing or migration paths are absent.
Runtime-only products have no compiler dependency or source-evaluation API.
Legacy aliases, loaders, translators, and compatibility entry points are absent.
Stale generation callbacks and destructor paths are absent.
High-risk parity tests have independent oracles.
VM-only feature matrices are absent.
Current public surfaces contain no universal bytecode promises or obsolete architecture diagrams.
Installed packages contain no retired headers, libraries, symbols, or cache directories.
Stale implementation targets are not presented as active architecture.
No known failure is masked by a skip, fallback, allowlist, or timeout exception.
Semantic, ownership, target, coroutine, and artifact verifiers have audited implementation independence.
Verifier normal and adversarial ladders satisfy hard time, memory, count, and worklist budgets.
Every invariant family has measured mutation coverage.
XSM and XTP decoders pass fuzzing and sanitizer gates with zero activation before verification.
Concurrency stress covers publication, final release, weak references, cancellation, waiters, generation changes, entry swaps, domain detach, and destruction.
Capability manifests state the exact OS and runtime enforcement boundary without claiming the compiler is a sandbox.
The trusted computing base explicitly inventories verifiers, typed execution, runtime kernels, enabled refinements, native emission, providers, and unsafe FFI.
The runtime ownership oracle declares its exact dynamic coverage boundary.
One mandatory semantic pipeline serves every supported execution route.
SemanticPlan and TargetPlan are immutable and independently verified before consumption.
VM and AOT consume the same plan fingerprint and pass symmetric conformance.
C emission consumes target facts and contains no analyzer semantics.
No legacy bytecode or public API compatibility path remains.
Typed execution does not default to DynValue and register representation is distinct from memory representation.
Materialized ABI, tags, layout, and extent have one canonical authority.
Ownership, exact balance, return provenance, roots, and cleanup are complete on every path.
AOT reference-count elimination proofs agree with runtime lifecycle oracles.
Generation unload cannot leave callable stale code.
Coroutine lowering is fully stackless with no hidden VM stack.
Deterministic and multiworker scheduling satisfy one frozen contract.
Each operation and complex kernel family has one semantic owner with no name dispatch.
XSM and XTP artifacts are deterministic and malformed input fails closed.
Runtime-only artifacts link and run without compiler or toolchain dependencies.
Typed and generic host calls consume the same call plan.
Target, provider, schema, capability, and fingerprint mismatches are rejected before activation.
Generation activation, drain, rollback, and unload pass retained stress evidence.
Sanitizer, fuzz, model, contract, portability, matrix, and performance gates all qualify.
Architecture, symbols, plan coverage, legacy residue, and dual-owner residue are terminal zero.
No unresolved known bug is hidden by a skip, fallback, allowlist, or compatibility route.
A machine-readable final manifest maps every completion item to evidence, command, result, and source identity.
Implementation identities and supported boundaries are synchronized across governed project surfaces.
Critical matrix and residue gates are replayed from an independent clean worktree before terminal publication.
Evidence distinguishes local, continuous-integration, and real-platform qualification from production release.
Integration-only install products and temporary caches are removed while governed benchmark, fuzz, and mutation artifacts remain auditable.
Every mandatory deletion inventory is terminal zero.
Every required completion assertion has current machine-verifiable evidence.
All prerequisite target-machine capabilities qualify with no deferred compatibility or fallback debt.
The full supported matrix passes positive activation and negative mismatch lanes.
Specifications, contracts, source, build, install, and runtime expose one architecture truth.
The final evidence package reproduces from its exact clean source identity.
The unified target-machine status is published as complete only after all preceding items qualify.
